rounds.pitch: This is a fictional practice pitch for testing, not actual company traction. Verdict helps first-time founders rehearse fundraising with an AI investor panel. Our initial buyers are university accelerators. In this hypothetical case, 3 accelerators tested it with 60 founders, 24 returned the next week, and 2 signed non-binding letters of intent at $200 per month. We use browser speech transcription and a shared conversation backend with four personas and at most two speakers per round. Technical expert and market researcher, please each ask your single most important unresolved question about reliability and customer demand. Interrogator and sympathizer can sit this round out.

responses.reason: Concrete, specific pilot numbers with clear prototype framing and an explicit request for reliability scrutiny; modest credit for a coherent, testable setup.
responses.reply: Browser speech transcription is the piece most likely to break in a live pitch, so what's your measured word error rate and end-to-end latency on real founder audio, not clean test recordings?

rounds.pitch: Continuing only the fictional test scenario: CTO, we tested 120 consented recordings of founders rehearsing in their usual rooms across six accent groups, rather than studio samples. Word error rate was 8% in quiet rooms and 18% in noisy rooms, with a 22% worst accent-group result. Median end-to-end time from the end of a sentence to its committed transcript was 0.9 seconds and p95 was 1.8 seconds. We restrict the pilot to quiet rooms, show transcripts for correction before submission, and request a repeat for dropped segments; dropped segments never trigger scoring. Market researcher, I cannot answer your question. I do not know whether any of the 24 founders returned voluntarily or under an accelerator requirement, and I have not identified the budget owner. I have no supporting evidence on either point yet.

responses.reason: Founder gave measured WER across accent groups and p50/p95 latency on real recordings, plus concrete mitigation for dropped segments; this directly clears my reliability concern.
responses.reply: Those numbers are credible and the correction step is a sensible mitigation, but a 22% worst-group error rate means some founders get a materially worse rehearsal, so how do you detect and handle that case in the pilot?
